title: Workers' Compensation Referral Registration: One Open Referral per Claim and Program
content:
# One open referral per claim and program

**Standard.** A worker may hold any number of Workers' Compensation Referral records over time, one per claim and program. A new referral is not opened when the worker already holds a referral that is not closed with the same claim number and the same program. A further program on the same claim — for example a Functional Capacity Evaluation during outpatient therapy, or Work Conditioning after it — is its own referral.

There is no fixed limit on how many referrals one worker may hold; the limit is on duplicates of the same claim and program.

## What decides a duplicate

| Element | What is compared |
|---|---|
| The worker | the same injured worker |
| The claim | the same carrier claim number |
| The program | the same program (for example Workers' Comp Outpatient Therapy) |
| The existing referral's status | any status other than closed: referral received, active, suspended or discharged |

The comparison is made on the referral records the system holds before the new referral is opened; it is the system record of the existing referral, not a caller's description of it, that counts. Only the claim number together with the program identifies the same referral.

## Cases (hypothetical)

- The worker holds a Workers' Comp Outpatient Therapy referral on claim A that is discharged but not yet closed. A second Workers' Comp Outpatient Therapy referral on claim A is not opened.
- The worker holds an active Workers' Comp Outpatient Therapy referral on claim A, and a Functional Capacity Evaluation is referred on the same claim. The evaluation is its own referral; this standard does not stand in its way.
- The worker holds an active Work Conditioning Program referral on claim A and is referred to Work Conditioning Program on a different claim B. The claim numbers differ, so the two are not duplicates.
